Configuration
Model
2D frame: one frame, with roof loads taken from the tributary width. 3D structure: the frame below repeats along the length of the canopy. The frames are tied together by eave beams along both roof edges and by any purlins you add, and the columns act as cantilevers for wind along the length (fixed bases).
Number of bays between frames along the canopy length. Frames = bays + 1.
Frame spacing (ft, center-to-center)
Edge / eave beams
Eave beams run the full length along the low and high roof edges and cantilever past the end frames to the front and back overhangs. No beams are added over the column lines; add purlins for any other longitudinal members. They are written to the MCT as AISC10(US) database sections.
Purlins (ft, plan distance from the low roof tip)
Fill evenly
Purlins run the full length on top of the frame beams, alongside the two eave beams. With at least one purlin, the roof dead, snow and wind loads go onto the purlins and eave beams by their tributary width across the roof. MIDAS then carries them into the frames, including the overhangs as cantilevers. With no purlins, roof loads go straight to the frames by tributary width. Fill evenly places that many purlins at equal spacing between the eaves.
Member end releases
Rafter ends at the eave beams
Eave beams at the frames
Purlins at the frames
A released end frees major and minor axis bending (My, Mz); torsion and shear stay connected. Pinned rafter: each frame beam is hinged to the low and high eave beams at its tips. Simple spans: the eave beams or purlins are hinged at every frame, except over an end frame with a front / back overhang, where the cantilever stays continuous with the first span. Where a pinned rafter meets a simple-span eave beam, the eave beam keeps its weak-axis (Mz) continuity on one side so the joint is not left free to spin; it carries no moment because nothing else at the joint resists that rotation. A pinned rafter tip also gets an RY support: the rafter's released rotation is the eave beam rolling about its own axis, so this torsional brace keeps the eave from spinning. It carries no moment for loads at the beam centroid.
Number of column lines supporting the roof beam. 1 = cantilever; 2 = simple bay; 3+ = multi-bay continuous canopy (statically indeterminate, solved by the in-app stiffness analysis).
Bay spacings (ft, center-to-center)
Center-to-center spacing of each bay between adjacent columns. The first column sits at the left overhang; the right overhang extends past the last column.
Column base elevations (ft)
Elevation of each column base (support), numbered left to right. Columns default to the datum (Base elevation in Geometry); enter a different value where a base steps up or down, e.g. a left column at -5 ft beside a right column at 0 ft. The roof stays where the datum and column height put it, so a lower base makes that column longer. Clear a box to return it to the datum.
Base elevation of every individual column: one row per frame (F1 at the front), one box per column line (A at the low side). Blank = the datum (Base elevation in Geometry). The roof stays where the datum and column height put it, so a lower base makes that column longer. A new frame copies the row before it.
Project information
These populate the page header of the Excel calc (Project / Subject / Task on the left, Computed and Checked by on the right) and the PDF report title block.
Column-to-beam connection
The roof beam is always continuous over the columns. This sets how each column connects to it. Fixed to beam: moment connection — the column and beam share rotation, so the beam transfers moment into the columns (typical welded/bolted-moment canopy). Pinned to beam: hinged connection — the column top is released, so it carries axial and shear but no moment from the beam. Affects how moment distributes to the columns.
Column base support condition for the MIDAS supports.

Used only to check the entered snow load against the ASCE 7-16 §7.3.4 minimum. It does not change the applied load.
ASCE 7-16 Ch. 7 inputs
Dead and snow are applied as uniform line loads (psf × tributary width) on the roof beam, vertical (global Z), defined over the horizontal projection (bPROJ=YES) per the ASCE snow convention. Self-weight is added automatically to the DL case in the MCT.

Dead & snow derivation

Wind — roof (ASCE 7-16)
Velocity pressure qₕ
Wind flow condition
Net roof pressure p = qₕ · G · C_N, with C_N from ASCE 7-16 Fig. 27.3-4 (monoslope free roof), interpolated at the roof angle.
Wind — columns & fascia
Fascia
Fascia wind pressure
Cf source
Which ASCE 7-16 table supplies Cf for the fascia. Fig. 29.4-1 treats the fascia as a flat-sided member and reads Cf from the aspect ratio (length/depth) at h/D = 1, 7, 25. Fig. 29.3-1 treats it as a solid sign and reads Cf from the aspect ratio B/s and clearance ratio s/h, where B = fascia length, s = fascia depth, and h = height to the top of the fascia. The sign provision generally governs for a shallow fascia high above grade.
Columns
Column wind pressure
Fascia lateral wind = fascia depth × pressure × tributary length, as a point load at the beam end. Column wind = pressure × projected column width, as a line load over the height. In Calculate mode the column pressure is derived as a flat-sided member per ASCE 7-16 §29.4 (Fig. 29.4-1, normal to face). The fascia pressure uses whichever Cf source is selected above — Fig. 29.4-1 (flat-sided member) or Fig. 29.3-1 (solid sign).
Windscreen
Screen wind pressure
Lateral screen wind applied as a uniform load over the screen height, on one column line. In Calculate mode the pressure is derived as a solid sign per ASCE 7-16 §29.3 (Fig 29.3-1 C_f from the screen's B/s and s/h), reduced for openings via §29.3.1 using the percent-open you enter.

Structural analysis

linear elastic · in-app
First-order linear elastic analysis of the generated MCT model, run in the browser: 3D beam elements with shear deformation (AISC shear areas), the same supports, end releases, load cases, combinations and envelope written to MIDAS. A 2D frame is solved as a plane frame. Results appear in the diagrams, reactions, report, Excel and DXF below, and update automatically when the model changes. No second-order (P-Delta) effects and no member design checks.

Whole structure — every frame, eave beam and purlin

Result Load
Coloured members: each member is coloured by the largest magnitude of the chosen result at either end of each element. Diagrams: the result is drawn along every member as in MIDAS (strong-axis results offset in the member's local z direction, weak-axis results in local y, same sign convention as the frame diagrams below); the envelope shows the max and min curves. Envelope = the governing value across all strength combinations. Hover a member or a diagram for the frame, element, end, value and governing combination. Reactions: support forces FX, FY, FZ (blue, single head, pointing the way the support pushes on the structure) and moments MX, MY, MZ (green, double head, right-hand rule) in global axes at every column base; for the envelope each component is its own governing value. Click a row in the frame table to show that frame in the diagrams below.

Column base reactions

awaiting MIDAS results
Member forces are as reported at the base; reactions are equal and opposite (what the foundation sees). Axis map: Axial → vertical (N), Shear-z → horizontal (V), Moment-y → base moment (M).
Run the in-app analysis above, or paste the MIDAS beam-force results, to read the column base reactions and free-body diagram.

Anchorage groups

base plate & anchor rods · AISC DG1 · ACI 318-19 Ch. 17
Each group is one base plate and anchorage detail, designed with the Base Plate & Anchor Bolt Designer (All-Structural). Assign columns to groups below: a group is checked for every LRFD combination at every column assigned to it, using the column base reactions from the analysis on the Results tab. Open a group to edit its plate, rods, concrete, grout and reinforcement in the full designer, print its report, or export it to Hilti PROFIS Engineering. The column section comes from the canopy model.

The title block uses the Project, Project no., Computed by and Checked by fields under Geometry → Project information.
